newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Panama officials discuss Howard base.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Panama officials discuss Howard base.

text.p: U.S. and Panamanian officials held informal talks in Miami on Monday on the proposed conversion of Howard Air Force Base in Panama into an international anti-drug centre with U.S. cooperation, the State Department said.

"The talks are another in a series of informal diplomatic exchanges between the United States and Panama on whether to convert the base and what part the United States might play," John McClenney, a State Department spokesman, told Reuters.
The United States is to turn over control of the Panama Canal to Panama and withdraw all troops and bases, including Howard base, by Dec. 31, 1999, in accordance with bilateral canal treaties.
Officials said Monday's talks included participation by John Negroponte, U.S. coordinator for the Panama bases negotiations, and Panamanian representative Jorge Ritter.
Negroponte chairs a U.S. Interagency Working Group on Panama, which is reviewing a possible post-1999 U.S. presence in that country.

Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares had said Panama would not enter into talks with the United States to negotiate a military presence in Panama in the next century. But he said Washington could keep Howard AFB at no cost for use as an anti-drug centre.

In Panama City, Foreign Ministry spokesman Erich Rodriguez said that the "routine talks" in Miami would involve the anti-drug centre proposal and Negroponte's planned retirement from the foreign service this summer should not effect the negotiations.
"The talks are between two countries, not two people," Rodriguez said.
